sources.title: 避難所運営等避難生活支援のためのガイドライン（チェックリスト）
sources.edition: 平成28年4月策定、令和6年12月改定
evidence_scope: 食料・物資管理、トイレ確保・管理、避難者の健康管理、配慮が必要な人への対応を避難所業務として整理
運営の各段階に必要な業務と連携体制を扱う
sources.limits: 運営上の確認事項を定めるガイドラインであり、個人の心理係数や施設の処理時間を測定した資料ではない。

sources.title: 避難所におけるトイレの確保・管理ガイドライン
sources.edition: 平成28年4月策定、令和6年12月改定
evidence_scope: 断水・停電・排水処理設備の破損・既設便器の被害により水洗トイレが利用できなくなる状況を整理
災害時のトイレ確保、管理、衛生、必要数の計画を扱う
sources.limits: 設備故障をシナリオに含める根拠として使う。故障の確率や一人当たりの所要時間は校正しない。

sources.title: 令和6年能登半島地震における避難所運営実態調査報告
sources.publisher: 内閣府政策統括官（防災担当）
sources.method: 奥能登4市町の5事例について、自治体職員、住民、NPO等にWeb会議または対面でヒアリング
evidence_scope: 避難所運営の主体、運営方法の移行、外部支援、役割分担、成功点と課題の事例
sources.limits: 事例ヒアリングであり、無作為抽出の標本や心理状態の測定ではない。個別事例から頻度や因果効果を推定しない。

values.direct_sleep_rest_stress_recovery: disabled; sleep debt and affect feedback retained
values.information_misinformation_uncertainty_p: active false-claim belief raises uncertainty through a per-minute assumption

assumptions.conceptual_reference: Kuppens et al. (2010), doi:10.1177/0956797610372634; existing life-state-feedback-v1 structure; neither source calibrates these coefficients
assumptions.calibration_status: uncalibrated integrated structure and ShelterSim assumptions
assumptions.notes: The policy integrates the exact acute mean-reversion step with the existing sleep-debt, uncertainty, reassurance, affect, hygiene, and discontent state. Social-model recovery and the legacy direct sleep/rest stress recovery are disabled in this composition to prevent duplicate recovery. Information correction is an event-level state change; persistent false belief acts through uncertainty once per tick as a level input, not as a replayed event pulse.
The event tests a documented category of service disruption. Its timing and two-stall magnitude are not claims about a particular disaster.
This event pins the replay contract only; its timing and magnitude are not a shelter or disaster assumption.

Quantities, warehouse/zone IDs and source IDs exercise inventory accounting only. The contextual source identifies the operational category and does not calibrate a consumption rate, warehouse layout or shelter stock level.
Event quantities and timing verify deterministic ledger behavior only; they are not empirical distribution or service assumptions.

values.reservation_order: scheduled event sequence then stable event ID
values.ownership: reservation is bound to one stable Agent ID

assumptions.notes: This assumption defines test event ordering and reservation ownership. It makes no claim about real allocation practice.
The serving quantity is a synthetic ledger test value, not a human intake estimate.

assumptions.target: SocialRuntimeLimits and event-triggered Haiku proposal policy
assumptions.notes: These limits select and bound optional model proposals. They are not a claim that a stress score of 0.65 has a validated real-world interpretation.

assumptions.target: SupportPriorityLimits for optional Haiku staff-queue priority requests
assumptions.notes: Units: stress score 0..1 and requests per simulated day. Requests below the threshold or over the daily cap keep the rule priority 0 without a provider call. The threshold reuses the social-proposal value for consistency; it is not a validated real-world urgency cutoff. support-priority-v1 histories keep their original every-request behavior for exact replay.

assumptions.target: Typed event effects for complaint response, same-group cooperation and information verification
assumptions.notes: These fixed effects make the event path testable; they are not measured estimates of human response. No generated dialogue or claim content is treated as fact.
Sources establish operational context only. They provide no normalized individual stress or need time series for estimating these rates.

Need pressure, queue wait and staff support wait are reported as separate direct contributions. Coefficients are bounded software hypotheses and are not clinical estimates or fitted to interview data.

values.high_distress_threshold_interpretation: internal simulation indicator only; not a clinical cutoff

assumptions.conceptual_reference: Kuppens et al. (2010), Emotional Inertia and Psychological Maladjustment, doi:10.1177/0956797610372634; Feelings Change, doi:10.1037/a0020962
assumptions.calibration_status: uncalibrated literature-inspired structure and software assumptions
assumptions.notes: The references motivate temporal persistence and recovery structure only. All rates, baselines, thresholds, and daily weights are ShelterSim assumptions, not estimates from those studies or shelter data.

The cited public sources do not measure contact-mediated stress transmission. All coefficients are invented for bounded software behavior tests and must not be read as empirical psychological effects.

values.travel_time_semantics: positive integer minutes supplied per zone edge; not measured walking speed
values.routing_policy: shortest total declared edge travel time; stable edge-ID tie-break
values.display_coordinates: presentation-only; never used in route calculation

assumptions.notes: These counts and travel times are fixture inputs, not recommendations or estimates of a real shelter.

values.assignment_order: priority requests first; ordinary requests are promoted after the configured wait and FIFO ordered by request minute then stable request ID; staff IDs break qualification ties

assumptions.notes: Sources describe staff roles and coordination, not request resolution duration, cooldown, or a validated fairness threshold. These values are experiment controls, not staffing guidance. Requests with no skill-qualified staff remain pending until their configured timeout; the run records the request-minute exposure.

sampling.mobility: categorical according to the template weights
sampling.numeric_attributes: independent keyed uniform values within each configured inclusive range
sampling.group_assignment: stable groups of template.group_size in generated profile order

assumptions.calibration_status: synthetic; not fitted to individuals or a shelter census
assumptions.notes: Template values and distributions are synthetic construction choices. Context sources identify operational needs only; they do not establish these distributions.
Synthetic coordinates are for display only and do not imply physical distance, adjacency or travel time.
The sources do not report sampled per-use service durations; the interval must not be described as measured.

eligibility_triggers.seek_help: support_need >= 0.25 and max(toilet_urgency, hunger, fatigue, stress) >= 0.50

values.choice: keyed-random softmax over eligible candidates; priorities add 0.5 before softmax

assumptions.notes: All weights, thresholds, intervals and priorities are rule assumptions; they are not estimated from interviews or measurements.

selection_order: keyed random choice for exact ties only

assumptions.notes: The ordering and shared utility values are software assumptions for sensitivity comparison. They do not predict real human choices or claim that priority is a preferred outcome.

assumptions.calibration_status: illustrative graph inputs and deterministic algorithm
assumptions.notes: Travel minutes are explicit fixture inputs. This is not a calibrated walking-speed or mobility-time estimate.

assumptions.target: SetZoneEdgeCommand and capacity-aware ZoneGraph routing for edited layout branches

values.capacity_semantics: maximum agents with a pending travel task on an edge
values.capacity_full: search an alternate route; otherwise record zone_edge_capacity_wait
values.facility_reachability: every zone must retain a route to every facility

assumptions.calibration_status: synthetic user-editable route and capacity assumptions
assumptions.notes: Edge travel minutes and transit capacities are explicit synthetic inputs, not measured walking speeds, facility flow rates or real shelter movement estimates.

values.queue_order: request minute then stable Agent ID
values.cancellation: release reservation once; suppress stale completion

assumptions.calibration_status: synthetic software test inputs and uncalibrated operational hypotheses
assumptions.notes: The operational source establishes the category of resource and service management only. Service time, resource quantities, need growth/relief, action thresholds/utilities, queue order and staff rules are implementation assumptions. The test quantities are not recommended stock levels or intake estimates.
These quantities exercise H02 reservation and consumption paths only. The operational source identifies resource management as a task and does not support these inventory values.

values.queue_policy: retain FIFO head and retry next tick
values.fixture_run_end: service due minute must be less than duration_minutes

assumptions.notes: Stall reasons, retry order and run-end behavior specify software observability and make no empirical claim about real queue policy or service availability.

values.shipment_delay: move pending delivery forward; preserve event ID and sequence
values.water_outage: block new water-service starts only; active services finish
values.staff_unavailable: release interrupted resource reservations once; requeue at prior FIFO arrival
values.event_trace: retain source_id and causation_id for applied, failed, and suppressed records

assumptions.calibration_status: deterministic software contract; no operational calibration
assumptions.notes: The operational source establishes only that resource and outage management are relevant shelter operations. Event timing, IDs, outage targets, staff availability intervals, and queue behavior in tests are synthetic assumptions, not measured availability or response-time evidence. A water outage does not directly add stress; unmet need follows the opted-in need policy.
These stock amounts exercise event, checkpoint, and service contracts. They are not a recommended shelter inventory or a human consumption estimate.
These times and the outage stall reason verify deterministic event and retry behavior only; they do not describe real delivery, outage, or staffing timelines.

assumptions.calibration_status: synthetic deterministic demo input; no operational calibration
assumptions.notes: Facility, staffing, population and duration values define a frozen demonstrator. The public guideline motivates studying resource and staff operations but does not establish these capacities or ratios.

assumptions.calibration_status: synthetic scenario quantities; not recommendations or consumption estimates
assumptions.notes: Stock values are selected to exercise ledger conservation, arrival delays, and queue response. They are not measured demand, safe minimum stock, or a recommended inventory.

assumptions.calibration_status: synthetic event schedule; no empirical timing or causal effect calibration
assumptions.notes: The times and intervention sizes create inspectable software test paths only. The operational guidance gives context for supply and water continuity, not these event timings or measured effects.

assumptions.calibration_status: synthetic intervention setting; not a real-world effect estimate
assumptions.notes: Typed intervention events restore a specific water outage or add food inventory to one new scenario run. KPI changes remain observations of one assumed simulation seed.

Contact and inquiry coefficients provide bounded, deterministic test behavior only. They do not estimate how frequently real people share or believe information, seek help, or respond to corrections. Simulation-side claim truth is separate from Agent belief.

values.paired_design: one parameter varies per case; all other inputs are held fixed

assumptions.calibration_status: reproducible synthetic software sensitivity protocol; not empirical calibration
assumptions.notes: The guideline supplies operational context only. Sensitivity values and the false-claim event schedule are software assumptions, selected before inspecting outcomes and never tuned to produce a preferred result. Three paired seeds provide descriptive variation, not a confidence interval or evidence about real shelter outcomes.

values.coefficients: ScenarioSpec model_configs; shared baseline parameter schemas

assumptions.conceptual_reference: McEwen (1998), Protective and Damaging Effects of Stress Mediators, doi:10.1056/NEJM199801153380307
assumptions.calibration_status: not empirically calibrated; literature-inspired operator adaptation
assumptions.notes: Experimental shelter adaptation, not measured. The reference motivates an operator, not the numerical coefficients or real-world validity.

values.formula: stress + alpha * mean(neighbor stress - stress); sparse sampled adaptation
values.coefficients: ScenarioSpec model_configs; shared baseline parameter schemas

assumptions.calibration_status: not empirically calibrated; literature-inspired operator adaptation
assumptions.notes: Experimental shelter adaptation, not measured. The reference motivates an operator, not the numerical coefficients or real-world validity.

values.contact_duration_semantics: eligibility threshold; not multiplied again into per-minute rate

assumptions.conceptual_reference: Bosse et al. (2013), Modelling collective decision making in groups and crowds, https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10458-012-9201-1; Bosse et al. (2015), Agent-Based Modelling of Emotion Contagion in Groups
assumptions.calibration_status: not empirically calibrated; expressiveness-channel-openness structure adapted for bounded shelter synchrony
assumptions.notes: Only the three-factor interaction structure is research-inspired. Channel weights, stress_sensitivity as openness, default expressiveness, and all numerical rates are ShelterSim assumptions; staff contacts and unsupplied relationships are not inferred.

values.formula: p=1-exp(-baseline transmission propensity); experimental hazard operator
values.coefficients: ScenarioSpec model_configs; shared baseline parameter schemas

assumptions.calibration_status: not empirically calibrated; literature-inspired operator adaptation
assumptions.notes: Experimental shelter adaptation, not measured. The reference motivates an operator, not the numerical coefficients or real-world validity.

assumptions.conceptual_reference: Daley & Kendall (1965), Stochastic Rumours, doi:10.1093/imamat/1.1.42; Nekovee et al. (2007), Theory of rumour spreading in complex social networks
assumptions.calibration_status: uncalibrated literature-inspired process structure and software assumptions
assumptions.notes: Exposure, belief strength, sharing propensity and correction acceptance are separate state/processes. References motivate spreading-process structure only; all shelter-specific probabilities and trust responses remain uncalibrated assumptions.
